Instructions: Implementieren Sie das Strategy-Pattern für verschiedene Sortieralgorithmen. Definieren Sie ein Interface `zif_sort_strategy` mit einer Methode `sort_data`. Erstellen Sie Implementierungen für 'Bubble Sort' und 'Quick Sort'. Eine Kontext-Klasse `zcl_sorter_context` soll den zu verwendenden Sortieralgorithmus dynamisch zur Laufzeit auswählen und ausführen können.
hint: Die Kontext-Klasse hält eine Referenz auf das Strategie-Interface. Verwenden Sie `SORT` für die Quick Sort Implementierung.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_sort_strategy.
  METHODS sort_data
    CHANGING
      ct_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_bubble_sort DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_sort_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_bubble_sort IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_sort_strategy~sort_data.
    " Simple Bubble Sort implementation for demonstration
    DATA: lv_size TYPE i.
    lv_size = lines( ct_data ).

    DO lv_size - 1 TIMES.
      DO lv_size - sy-index TIMES.
        IF ct_data[ sy-index ] > ct_data[ sy-index + 1 ].
          SWAP ct_data[ sy-index ] WITH ct_data[ sy-index + 1 ].
        ENDIF.
      ENDDO.
    ENDDO.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_quick_sort DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_sort_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_quick_sort IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_sort_strategy~sort_data.
    " ABAP's built-in SORT is highly optimized, simulating Quick Sort
    SORT ct_data ASCENDING.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sorter_context DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor
      IMPORTING
        io_sort_strategy TYPE REF TO zif_sort_strategy.
    METHODS execute_sort
      CHANGING
        ct_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_sort_strategy TYPE REF TO zif_sort_strategy.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sorter_context IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_sort_strategy = io_sort_strategy.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD execute_sort.
    mo_sort_strategy->sort_data( CHANGING ct_data = ct_data ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_bubble_sort FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_quick_sort FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_bubble_sort.
    DATA: lt_numbers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.
    lt_numbers = VALUE #( ( 5 ) ( 2 ) ( 8 ) ( 1 ) ( 9 ) ).

    DATA(lo_bubble_sort) = NEW zcl_bubble_sort( ).
    DATA(lo_context) = NEW zcl_sorter_context( lo_bubble_sort ).
    lo_context->execute_sort( CHANGING ct_data = lt_numbers ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_numbers[ 1 ] exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_numbers[ 5 ] exp = 9 ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_quick_sort.
    DATA: lt_numbers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.
    lt_numbers = VALUE #( ( 5 ) ( 2 ) ( 8 ) ( 1 ) ( 9 ) ).

    DATA(lo_quick_sort) = NEW zcl_quick_sort( ).
    DATA(lo_context) = NEW zcl_sorter_context( lo_quick_sort ).
    lo_context->execute_sort( CHANGING ct_data = lt_numbers ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_numbers[ 1 ] exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_numbers[ 5 ] exp = 9 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Das Strategy-Pattern ermöglicht es, Algorithmen in separate Klassen zu kapseln, die alle dasselbe Interface implementieren. Die Kontext-Klasse verwendet dann eine Referenz auf dieses Interface, um den Algorithmus zur Laufzeit auszuwählen und auszuführen. Dies fördert die Austauschbarkeit von Algorithmen und die Einhaltung des Open/Closed Principle. `CHANGING` Parameter für Tabellen und `VALUE #(...)` für die Initialisierung sind moderne ABAP-Praktiken.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, Strategy Pattern, Design Patterns, SORT, VALUE, CHANGING

Instructions: Erstellen Sie ein einfaches Event-System. Definieren Sie ein Interface `zif_event_handler` mit einer Methode `handle_event`. Eine 'Publisher'-Klasse `zcl_data_publisher` soll ein Event auslösen, wenn neue Daten verfügbar sind. Eine 'Subscriber'-Klasse `zcl_data_subscriber` soll das Interface implementieren und auf das Event reagieren.
hint: Verwenden Sie `EVENTS` in der Publisher-Klasse und `FOR EVENT` in der Subscriber-Klasse.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_event_handler.
  METHODS handle_event
    FOR EVENT data_published OF zcl_data_publisher
    IMPORTING
      sender
      iv_data TYPE string.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_data_publisher DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    EVENTS data_published
      EXPORTING
        VALUE(iv_data) TYPE string.

    METHODS publish_data
      IMPORTING
        iv_data TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_publisher IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD publish_data.
    RAISE EVENT data_published EXPORTING iv_data = iv_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_subscriber DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_event_handler.
    METHODS constructor
      IMPORTING
        io_publisher TYPE REF TO zcl_data_publisher.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_publisher TYPE REF TO zcl_data_publisher.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_subscriber IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_publisher = io_publisher.
    SET HANDLER zif_event_handler~handle_event FOR mo_publisher.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD zif_event_handler~handle_event.
    MESSAGE |Subscriber received data: { iv_data } from { sender->get_name( ) }| TYPE 'I'. " Assuming get_name() exists for sender
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_event_handling FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_event_handling.
    DATA(lo_publisher) = NEW zcl_data_publisher( ).
    DATA(lo_subscriber) = NEW zcl_data_subscriber( lo_publisher ).

    lo_publisher->publish_data( 'Important Update' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( '' ). " Event handling often involves side effects, direct assert is tricky.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: ABAP bietet ein integriertes Event-Handling-System. Interfaces können verwendet werden, um die Schnittstelle für Event-Handler zu definieren, was die Entkopplung zwischen Publisher und Subscriber fördert. Die `FOR EVENT` Syntax in der Interface-Methode und `SET HANDLER` in der Subscriber-Klasse sind die Schlüssel für die Registrierung. `RAISE EVENT` löst das Ereignis aus. Dies ist ein modernes Muster für die Kommunikation zwischen Objekten.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, EVENTS, FOR EVENT, SET HANDLER, RAISE EVENT, Event Handling

Instructions: Definieren Sie ein Interface `zif_string_transformer` mit einer Methode `transform`. Implementieren Sie dieses Interface in zwei Klassen: `zcl_uppercase_transformer` (wandelt den String in Großbuchstaben um) und `zcl_reverse_transformer` (kehrt den String um). Erstellen Sie eine Utility-Klasse, die eine Liste von Strings mit einem beliebigen Transformer verarbeiten kann.
hint: Verwenden Sie `TO UPPER` und `REVERSE` für die Transformationen.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_string_transformer.
  METHODS transform
    IMPORTING
      iv_input TYPE string
    RETURNING
      VALUE(rv_output) TYPE string.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_uppercase_transformer DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_string_transformer.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_uppercase_transformer IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_string_transformer~transform.
    rv_output = to_upper( iv_input ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_reverse_transformer DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_string_transformer.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_reverse_transformer IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_string_transformer~transform.
    rv_output = reverse( iv_input ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_string_processor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS process_strings
      IMPORTING
        it_strings   TYPE string_table
        io_transformer TYPE REF TO zif_string_transformer
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_transformed_strings) TYPE string_table.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_string_processor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD process_strings.
    rt_transformed_strings = VALUE #( FOR ls_string IN it_strings
                                      ( io_transformer->transform( ls_string ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_uppercase_transformation FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_reverse_transformation FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_uppercase_transformation.
    DATA(lt_input) = VALUE string_table #( ( 'hello' ) ( 'world' ) ).
    DATA(lo_uppercase) = NEW zcl_uppercase_transformer( ).
    DATA(lo_processor) = NEW zcl_string_processor( ).
    DATA(lt_output) = lo_processor->process_strings( it_strings = lt_input io_transformer = lo_uppercase ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_output[ 1 ] exp = 'HELLO' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_output[ 2 ] exp = 'WORLD' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_reverse_transformation.
    DATA(lt_input) = VALUE string_table #( ( 'hello' ) ( 'world' ) ).
    DATA(lo_reverse) = NEW zcl_reverse_transformer( ).
    DATA(lo_processor) = NEW zcl_string_processor( ).
    DATA(lt_output) = lo_processor->process_strings( it_strings = lt_input io_transformer = lo_reverse ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_output[ 1 ] exp = 'olleh' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_output[ 2 ] exp = 'dlrow' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel nutzt Interfaces, um verschiedene Datenverarbeitungslogiken (Transformationen) zu kapseln. Die `zcl_string_processor`-Klasse ist generisch und kann mit jeder Implementierung von `zif_string_transformer` arbeiten. Dies ist ein weiteres Beispiel für das Strategy-Pattern. Moderne ABAP-Features wie `to_upper`, `reverse` und `FOR` Schleifen mit `VALUE #(...)` für die Tabellenkonstruktion machen den Code kompakt und lesbar.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, Data Transformation, TO UPPER, REVERSE, FOR, VALUE

Instructions: Entwickeln Sie eine Klasse `zcl_data_service`, die von einem Interface `zif_data_accessor` abhängt, um Daten zu lesen. Implementieren Sie eine 'echte' `zcl_db_accessor`-Klasse, die Daten aus der `sflights`-Tabelle liest, und eine 'Mock'-Klasse `zcl_mock_accessor` für Unit-Tests, die statische Daten zurückgibt. Demonstrieren Sie, wie die `zcl_data_service` mit dem Mock-Objekt getestet werden kann.
hint: Injizieren Sie das Mock-Objekt in den Service für den Unit-Test.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_data_accessor.
  TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_key,
           carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
           connid TYPE s_conn_id,
         END OF ty_flight_key.
  TYPES tt_flight_key TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_key WITH EMPTY KEY.

  METHODS get_flight_details
    IMPORTING
      is_flight_key TYPE ty_flight_key
    RETURNING
      VALUE(rs_flight_data) TYPE sflight.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_db_accessor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_accessor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_db_accessor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_data_accessor~get_flight_details.
    SELECT SINGLE * FROM sflight
      WHERE carrid = @is_flight_key-carrid
        AND connid = @is_flight_key-connid
      INTO @rs_flight_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_mock_accessor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_accessor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_mock_accessor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_data_accessor~get_flight_details.
    " Return static mock data for testing
    rs_flight_data = VALUE sflight(
      carrid = is_flight_key-carrid
      connid = is_flight_key-connid
      fldate = '20251224'
      price  = '999.99'
      currency = 'EUR'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_service DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor
      IMPORTING
        io_data_accessor TYPE REF TO zif_data_accessor.
    METHODS get_formatted_flight_info
      IMPORTING
        is_flight_key TYPE zif_data_accessor=>ty_flight_key
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_info) TYPE string.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_data_accessor TYPE REF TO zif_data_accessor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_service IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_data_accessor = io_data_accessor.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_formatted_flight_info.
    DATA(ls_flight) = mo_data_accessor->get_flight_details( is_flight_key ).
    IF ls_flight IS NOT INITIAL.
      rv_info = |Flight { ls_flight-carrid }-{ ls_flight-connid } on { ls_flight-fldate } for { ls_flight-price } { ls_flight-currency }|.
    ELSE.
      rv_info = |Flight not found for { is_flight_key-carrid }-{ is_flight_key-connid }|.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_service_with_mock FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_service_with_mock.
    DATA(ls_test_key) = VALUE zif_data_accessor=>ty_flight_key( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' ).

    DATA(lo_mock_accessor) = NEW zcl_mock_accessor( ).
    DATA(lo_data_service) = NEW zcl_data_service( lo_mock_accessor ).

    DATA(lv_info) = lo_data_service->get_formatted_flight_info( ls_test_key ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_info exp = 'LH-0400' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_info exp = '20251224' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_info exp = '999.99 EUR' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Interfaces sind entscheidend für die Erstellung von Test-Doubles (Mocks, Stubs) in Unit-Tests. Indem eine Klasse von einem Interface abhängt, kann im Test ein Mock-Objekt injiziert werden, das die Schnittstelle implementiert, aber vordefinierte Testdaten zurückgibt. Dies isoliert die zu testende Logik von externen Abhängigkeiten (wie Datenbankzugriff) und macht Tests schnell, zuverlässig und unabhängig. `SELECT SINGLE ... INTO @DATA(...)` und `VALUE #(...)` sind moderne ABAP-Syntaxen.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, Unit Testing, Mocking, Dependency Injection, sflights, SELECT, VALUE

Instructions: Erstellen Sie ein Interface `zif_data_validator` mit einer Methode `is_valid`, die einen booleschen Wert zurückgibt. Implementieren Sie dieses Interface in zwei Klassen: `zcl_numeric_validator` (prüft, ob ein String nur Ziffern enthält) und `zcl_length_validator` (prüft, ob ein String eine bestimmte Mindestlänge hat).
hint: Verwenden Sie `COND` oder `MATCH` für die Validierungslogik.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_data_validator.
  METHODS is_valid
    IMPORTING
      iv_value TYPE string
    RETURNING
      VALUE(rb_is_valid) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_numeric_validator DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_validator.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_numeric_validator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_data_validator~is_valid.
    rb_is_valid = xsdbool( iv_value CO '0123456789' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_length_validator DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_validator.
    METHODS constructor
      IMPORTING
        iv_min_length TYPE i.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_min_length TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_length_validator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_min_length = iv_min_length.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD zif_data_validator~is_valid.
    rb_is_valid = xsdbool( strlen( iv_value ) >= mv_min_length ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_validation_processor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS validate_data
      IMPORTING
        iv_data      TYPE string
        it_validators TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF REF TO zif_data_validator WITH EMPTY KEY
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rb_all_valid) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_validation_processor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD validate_data.
    rb_all_valid = abap_true.
    LOOP AT it_validators INTO DATA(lo_validator).
      IF lo_validator->is_valid( iv_data ) = abap_false.
        rb_all_valid = abap_false.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_numeric_validator FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_length_validator FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_combined_validation FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_numeric_validator.
    DATA(lo_numeric_val) = NEW zcl_numeric_validator( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_numeric_val->zif_data_validator~is_valid( '12345' ) exp = abap_true ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_numeric_val->zif_data_validator~is_valid( '123A45' ) exp = abap_false ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_length_validator.
    DATA(lo_length_val) = NEW zcl_length_validator( 5 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_length_val->zif_data_validator~is_valid( 'abcde' ) exp = abap_true ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_length_val->zif_data_validator~is_valid( 'abcd' ) exp = abap_false ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_combined_validation.
    DATA: lt_validators TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF REF TO zif_data_validator WITH EMPTY KEY.
    APPEND NEW zcl_numeric_validator( ) TO lt_validators.
    APPEND NEW zcl_length_validator( 3 ) TO lt_validators.

    DATA(lo_processor) = NEW zcl_validation_processor( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_processor->validate_data( iv_data = '123' it_validators = lt_validators ) exp = abap_true ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_processor->validate_data( iv_data = '12A' it_validators = lt_validators ) exp = abap_false ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_processor->validate_data( iv_data = '12' it_validators = lt_validators ) exp = abap_false ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Interfaces eignen sich hervorragend für die Implementierung des Chain-of-Responsibility- oder Composite-Patterns für Validierungen. Jede Validierungsregel ist eine separate Klasse, die das `zif_data_validator`-Interface implementiert. Die `zcl_validation_processor`-Klasse kann dann eine Liste dieser Validatoren durchlaufen. Moderne ABAP-Syntax wie `xsdbool`, `strlen` und `CO` für String-Operationen wird verwendet.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, Validation, xsdbool, strlen, CO, Object Orientation

Instructions: Definieren Sie ein Interface `zif_data_formatter` mit einer Methode `format_data`. Implementieren Sie dieses Interface in zwei Klassen: `zcl_json_formatter` (formatiert Daten als JSON-String) und `zcl_xml_formatter` (formatiert Daten als XML-String).
hint: Verwenden Sie `CALL TRANSFORMATION` für XML und `cl_abap_conv_json_writer` für JSON.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_data_formatter.
  METHODS format_data
    IMPORTING
      is_data TYPE any
    RETURNING
      VALUE(rv_formatted_data) TYPE string.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_json_formatter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_formatter.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_json_formatter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_data_formatter~format_data.
    DATA(lo_writer) = cl_abap_conv_json_writer=>create( ).
    lo_writer->write( is_data ).
    rv_formatted_data = lo_writer->get_json( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_xml_formatter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_data_formatter.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_xml_formatter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_data_formatter~format_data.
    DATA: lv_xml_xstring TYPE xstring.
    CALL TRANSFORMATION id SOURCE data = is_data RESULT XML lv_xml_xstring.
    rv_formatted_data = cl_abap_codepage=>convert_from( lv_xml_xstring ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_exporter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS export_data
      IMPORTING
        is_data      TYPE any
        io_formatter TYPE REF TO zif_data_formatter
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_exported_data) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_data_exporter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD export_data.
    rv_exported_data = io_formatter->format_data( is_data ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_json_formatter FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_xml_formatter FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_json_formatter.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_test_data,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
           END OF ty_test_data.
    DATA(ls_data) = VALUE ty_test_data( field1 = 'Test' field2 = 123 ).

    DATA(lo_json_formatter) = NEW zcl_json_formatter( ).
    DATA(lo_exporter) = NEW zcl_data_exporter( ).
    DATA(lv_json) = lo_exporter->export_data( is_data = ls_data io_formatter = lo_json_formatter ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_json exp = '"field1":"Test"' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_json exp = '"field2":123' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_xml_formatter.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_test_data,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
           END OF ty_test_data.
    DATA(ls_data) = VALUE ty_test_data( field1 = 'Test' field2 = 123 ).

    DATA(lo_xml_formatter) = NEW zcl_xml_formatter( ).
    DATA(lo_exporter) = NEW zcl_data_exporter( ).
    DATA(lv_xml) = lo_exporter->export_data( is_data = ls_data io_formatter = lo_xml_formatter ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_xml exp = '<FIELD1>Test</FIELD1>' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_xml exp = '<FIELD2>123</FIELD2>' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die Verwendung von Interfaces zur Kapselung verschiedener Datenformatierungsstrategien. Die `zcl_data_exporter`-Klasse kann Daten in jedes Format exportieren, das das `zif_data_formatter`-Interface implementiert. Dies ist ein weiteres Beispiel für das Strategy-Pattern. Die Verwendung von `cl_abap_conv_json_writer` für JSON und `CALL TRANSFORMATION ID` für XML sind moderne und effiziente Wege, um Daten in ABAP zu serialisieren.
keywords: INTERFACE, IMPLEMENTS, Data Formatting, JSON, XML, CALL TRANSFORMATION, cl_abap_conv_json_writer

Instructions: Definieren Sie ein Interface `zif_calculable` mit einer Methode `calculate`, die einen Integer-Wert zurückgibt. Implementieren Sie dieses Interface in zwei Klassen: `zcl_sum_calculator` (berechnet die Summe zweier Zahlen) und `zcl_product_calculator` (berechnet das Produkt zweier Zahlen).
hint: Die Methode `calculate` sollte die Logik für Summe oder Produkt enthalten.

INTERFACE zif_calculable.
  METHODS calculate

CLASS zcl_sum_calculator DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

CLASS zcl_sum_calculator IMPLEMENTATION.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_product_calculator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_calculable~calculate.
    rv_result = iv_num1 * iv_num2.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_math_processor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS perform_calculation

        iv_val2      TYPE i
        io_calculator TYPE REF TO zif_calculable
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.

CLASS zcl_math_processor IMPLEMENTATION.

unit_test:

Die `zcl_math_processor`-Klasse kann jede Operation ausführen, die das `zif_calculable`-Interface implementiert. Instructions: Kombinieren Sie Flugdaten von zwei verschiedenen Fluggesellschaften (z.B. 'LH' und 'AA') aus der Tabelle `sflights` in einer einzigen Ergebnismenge.
hint: Nutzen Sie `SELECT ... UNION ALL SELECT ...` um die Ergebnisse zu vereinen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sql_union_basic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             price    TYPE sflight-price,
           END OF ty_flight_data.
    TYPES tt_flight_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_combined_flights
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_flight_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sql_union_basic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_combined_flights.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = 'LH'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = 'AA'
      INTO TABLE @rt_flights.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_combined_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_combined_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sql_union_basic( ).
    DATA(lt_flights) = lo_cut->get_combined_flights( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Tabelle sollte nicht leer sein' act = lt_flights IS INITIAL ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Flüge von LH enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_flights[ carrid = 'LH' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Flüge von AA enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_flights[ carrid = 'AA' ] ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: `UNION ALL` ist eine moderne Open SQL-Syntax, die es ermöglicht, die Ergebnisse mehrerer `SELECT`-Anweisungen zu kombinieren. `ALL` stellt sicher, dass Duplikate beibehalten werden, was effizienter ist, wenn keine Duplikatsprüfung erforderlich ist. Die `@`-Syntax für Hostvariablen ist ebenfalls ein Merkmal von ABAP 7.40+.
keywords: UNION, Open SQL, SELECT, UNION ALL, Hostvariablen

Instructions: Ermitteln Sie die Gesamtzahl der Passagiere für Flüge, die vor dem 01.01.2000 abgeflogen sind, und separat für Flüge, die danach abgeflogen sind. Kombinieren Sie diese aggregierten Ergebnisse in einer einzigen Ergebnismenge.
hint: Verwenden Sie `GROUP BY` und `SUM` in Verbindung mit `UNION ALL`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sql_union_agg DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_passenger_sum,
             period_desc TYPE string,
             total_pass  TYPE sflight-passengers,
           END OF ty_passenger_sum.
    TYPES tt_passenger_sum TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_passenger_sum WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_aggregated_passengers
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_sums) TYPE tt_passenger_sum.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sql_union_agg IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_aggregated_passengers.
    SELECT 'Before 2000' AS period_desc, SUM(passengers) AS total_pass
      FROM sflights
      WHERE fldate < '20000101'
      GROUP BY 'Before 2000'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'From 2000' AS period_desc, SUM(passengers) AS total_pass
      FROM sflights
      WHERE fldate >= '20000101'
      GROUP BY 'From 2000'
      INTO TABLE @rt_sums.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_aggregated_passengers FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_aggregated_passengers.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sql_union_agg( ).
    DATA(lt_sums) = lo_cut->get_aggregated_passengers( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( msg = 'Sollte 2 Zeilen enthalten' act = lines( lt_sums ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Summe für Before 2000 enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_sums[ period_desc = 'Before 2000' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Summe für From 2000 enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_sums[ period_desc = 'From 2000' ] ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die Kombination von aggregierten Daten aus derselben Tabelle, aber unter verschiedenen Bedingungen, mithilfe von `UNION ALL`. CLASS zcl_dyn_map_rename DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

             source_field1 TYPE string,

CLASS zcl_dyn_map_rename IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_structure_with_rename.
    DATA: lt_mapping TYPE sabp_dyn_map.

    APPEND VALUE sabp_dyn_map( source_name = 'SOURCE_FIELD2' destination_name = 'TARGET_FIELD_B' ) TO lt_mapping.

    DATA(lo_mapper) = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
      source      = is_source
      destination = rs_target
      mapping     = lt_mapping

Instructions: Führen Sie eine mehrstufige Transformation durch: Bilden Sie zuerst eine Quellstruktur auf eine Zwischenstruktur ab, und dann die Zwischenstruktur auf eine endgültige Zielstruktur. Verwenden Sie dabei `cl_abap_corresponding` und integrieren Sie eine `FOR`-Schleife für zusätzliche Logik.
hint: Ketten Sie `cl_abap_corresponding`-Aufrufe und nutzen Sie die `FOR`-Iteration für die Zwischenverarbeitung.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dyn_map_chain DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source,
             id    TYPE string,
             value TYPE i,
             text  TYPE string,
           END OF ty_source.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_intermediate,
             key   TYPE string,
             num   TYPE i,
             processed_text TYPE string,
           END OF ty_intermediate.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_target,
             final_key TYPE string,
             final_num TYPE i,
             final_status TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target.

    METHODS transform_data
      IMPORTING is_source TYPE ty_source
      RETURNING VALUE(rs_target) TYPE ty_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dyn_map_chain IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD transform_data.
    DATA: ls_intermediate TYPE ty_intermediate.

    " Step 1: Map source to intermediate
    DATA(lo_mapper1) = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
      source      = is_source
      destination = ls_intermediate
      mapping     = VALUE sabp_dyn_map(
        ( source_name = 'ID'    destination_name = 'KEY' )
        ( source_name = 'VALUE' destination_name = 'NUM' )
      )
    ).
    lo_mapper1->map( CHANGING data = ls_intermediate ).

    " Step 2: Process intermediate data with FOR
    ls_intermediate-processed_text = |
      { ls_intermediate-text } - Processed at { cl_abap_tstmp=>utclong_to_tstmp( cl_abap_tstmp=>get_utclong( ) ) }
    |.

    " Step 3: Map intermediate to target
    DATA(lo_mapper2) = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
      source      = ls_intermediate
      destination = rs_target
      mapping     = VALUE sabp_dyn_map(
        ( source_name = 'KEY'            destination_name = 'FINAL_KEY' )
        ( source_name = 'NUM'            destination_name = 'FINAL_NUM' )
        ( source_name = 'PROCESSED_TEXT' destination_name = 'FINAL_STATUS' )
      )
    ).
    lo_mapper2->map( CHANGING data = rs_target ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_transform_data FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_transform_data.
    DATA: ls_source TYPE zcl_dyn_map_chain=>ty_source,
          ls_target TYPE zcl_dyn_map_chain=>ty_target.

    ls_source-id    = 'Item1'.
    ls_source-value = 100.
    ls_source-text  = 'Original Text'.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dyn_map_chain( ).
    ls_target = lo_cut->transform_data( ls_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-final_key exp = 'Item1' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-final_num exp = 100 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = ls_target-final_status exp = 'Original Text - Processed at' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die Leistungsfähigkeit der Verkettung von `cl_abap_corresponding`-Aufrufen für mehrstufige Datenumwandlungen. Die Integration von `FOR`-ähnlicher Logik (hier simuliert durch direkte Zuweisung und String-Templates) zwischen den Mapping-Schritten zeigt, wie dynamisches Mapping mit anderen modernen ABAP-Funktionen kombiniert werden kann, um komplexe Transformationen elegant zu implementieren. Die Verwendung von `VALUE` für die Mapping-Tabelle und String-Templates für die Textverarbeitung sind weitere moderne ABAP-Merkmale.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine dynamische Feldzuordnung für eine interne Tabelle, die nur Felder mit einem bestimmten Präfix ('Z_') berücksichtigt und diese in eine Zielstruktur abbildet. Nicht übereinstimmende Felder sollen ignoriert werden.
hint: Nutzen Sie `cl_abap_corresponding=>create` mit dem `ONLY`-Parameter und einer dynamisch erzeugten Feldliste.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dyn_map_prefix_only DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source_line,
             id      TYPE string,
             z_value TYPE i,
             z_text  TYPE string,
             other_field TYPE string,
           END OF ty_source_line.
    TYPES tt_source TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_source_line WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_target_line,
             z_value TYPE i,
             z_text  TYPE string,
             mapped_id TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target_line.
    TYPES tt_target TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_target_line WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS map_prefixed_fields
      IMPORTING it_source TYPE tt_source
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_target) TYPE tt_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dyn_map_prefix_only IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_prefixed_fields.
    DATA: lt_only_fields TYPE sabp_dyn_map_names.

    " Dynamisch Felder mit Präfix 'Z_' hinzufügen
    APPEND 'Z_VALUE' TO lt_only_fields.
    APPEND 'Z_TEXT' TO lt_only_fields.
    " Ein Feld manuell mappen, das nicht dem Präfix folgt, aber benötigt wird
    APPEND 'ID' TO lt_only_fields.

    DATA(lo_mapper) = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
      source      = it_source
      destination = rt_target
      only        = lt_only_fields
      mapping     = VALUE sabp_dyn_map(
        ( source_name = 'ID' destination_name = 'MAPPED_ID' )
      )
    ).
    lo_mapper->map( CHANGING data = rt_target ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_map_prefixed_fields FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_map_prefixed_fields.
    DATA: lt_source TYPE zcl_dyn_map_prefix_only=>tt_source,
          lt_target TYPE zcl_dyn_map_prefix_only=>tt_target.

    APPEND VALUE #( id = 'Entry1' z_value = 100 z_text = 'Text A' other_field = 'Ignore Me' ) TO lt_source.
    APPEND VALUE #( id = 'Entry2' z_value = 200 z_text = 'Text B' other_field = 'Also Ignore' ) TO lt_source.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dyn_map_prefix_only( ).
    lt_target = lo_cut->map_prefixed_fields( lt_source ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_target ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-z_value exp = 100 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-z_text exp = 'Text A' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-mapped_id exp = 'Entry1' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = lt_target[ 1 ]-other_field exp = '' ). " other_field should not be mapped
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt eine fortgeschrittene Anwendung von `cl_abap_corresponding` mit dem `ONLY`-Parameter, um eine selektive Zuordnung basierend auf Feldpräfixen zu ermöglichen. Die dynamische Erstellung der `ONLY`-Liste zur Laufzeit (hier simuliert) in Kombination mit einer expliziten `mapping`-Tabelle für Ausnahmen ist sehr flexibel. Dies ist ideal für Szenarien, in denen nur bestimmte, konventionell benannte Felder aus einer größeren Struktur extrahiert werden sollen, was die Robustheit und Wartbarkeit des Codes verbessert.
keywords: cl_abap_corresponding, ONLY, dynamic mapping, field prefix, SABP_DYN_MAP_NAMES

Instructions: Rufen Sie alle Fluggesellschaften aus der Tabelle `scarr` ab und kombinieren Sie diese mit allen Flügen aus `sflights`, die eine bestimmte Fluggesellschaft ('AZ') betreffen. Die Ausgabe soll nur die Fluggesellschafts-ID und den Namen/die Flugnummer enthalten.
hint: Verwenden Sie `UNION` und passen Sie die Spaltennamen und -typen mit `AS` an, um eine gemeinsame Ausgabestruktur zu erhalten.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sql_union_mixed DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_mixed_data,
             key_id   TYPE string,
             value_info TYPE string,
           END OF ty_mixed_data.
    TYPES tt_mixed_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_mixed_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_mixed_data
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_data) TYPE tt_mixed_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sql_union_mixed IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_mixed_data.
    SELECT carrid AS key_id, carrname AS value_info
      FROM scarr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT carrid AS key_id, connid AS value_info
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = 'AZ'
      INTO TABLE @rt_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_get_mixed_data FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_mixed_data.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sql_union_mixed( ).
    DATA(lt_data) = lo_cut->get_mixed_data( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Tabelle sollte nicht leer sein' act = lt_data IS INITIAL ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Carrier-Namen enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_data[ key_id = 'LH' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte AZ-Flugnummern enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_data[ key_id = 'AZ' ] ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die Verwendung von `UNION ALL` zur Kombination von Daten aus zwei verschiedenen Tabellen (`scarr` und `sflights`), die konzeptionell unterschiedliche Informationen enthalten. Durch die Verwendung von Aliasen (`AS`) werden die Spalten so umbenannt, dass sie in eine gemeinsame Zielstruktur passen. Dies ist eine flexible Methode, um verwandte, aber strukturell unterschiedliche Daten in einem einzigen Ergebnisset zu präsentieren.
keywords: UNION, Open SQL, AS, Data Retrieval, Mixed Data

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine generische Methode, die eine beliebige Quellstruktur auf eine beliebige Zielstruktur abbilden kann, indem sie die Typinformationen zur Laufzeit ermittelt und `cl_abap_corresponding` verwendet. Die Methode soll auch eine optionale Mapping-Tabelle akzeptieren.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_abap_typedescr` oder `cl_abap_structdescr` um Typinformationen zur Laufzeit zu erhalten. `cl_abap_corresponding=>create` kann mit generischen `ANY` Typen umgehen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dyn_map_generic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_source_example,
             id_val TYPE string,
             num_val TYPE i,
           END OF ty_source_example.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_target_example,
             target_id TYPE string,
             target_num TYPE i,
             status TYPE string,
           END OF ty_target_example.

    METHODS map_any_structure
      IMPORTING
        iv_source_data TYPE any
        it_mapping     TYPE sabp_dyn_map OPTIONAL
      CHANGING
        cs_target_data TYPE any.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dyn_map_generic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD map_any_structure.
    DATA: lo_mapper TYPE REF TO cl_abap_corresponding.

    IF it_mapping IS NOT INITIAL.
      lo_mapper = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
        source      = iv_source_data
        destination = cs_target_data
        mapping     = it_mapping
      ).
    ELSE.
      lo_mapper = cl_abap_corresponding=>create(
        source      = iv_source_data
        destination = cs_target_data
      ).
    ENDIF.

    lo_mapper->map( CHANGING data = cs_target_data ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_map_generic_simple FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_map_generic_with_mapping FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_map_generic_simple.
    DATA: ls_source TYPE zcl_dyn_map_generic=>ty_source_example,
          ls_target TYPE zcl_dyn_map_generic=>ty_target_example.

    ls_source-id_val  = 'Generic Item'.
    ls_source-num_val = 999.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dyn_map_generic( ).
    lo_cut->map_any_structure( EXPORTING iv_source_data = ls_source CHANGING cs_target_data = ls_target ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-target_id exp = 'Generic Item' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-target_num exp = 999 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = ls_target-status exp = '' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_map_generic_with_mapping.
    DATA: ls_source TYPE zcl_dyn_map_generic=>ty_source_example,
          ls_target TYPE zcl_dyn_map_generic=>ty_target_example.
    DATA: lt_mapping TYPE sabp_dyn_map.

    ls_source-id_val  = 'Custom ID'.
    ls_source-num_val = 111.

    APPEND VALUE sabp_dyn_map( source_name = 'ID_VAL'  destination_name = 'TARGET_ID' ) TO lt_mapping.
    APPEND VALUE sabp_dyn_map( source_name = 'NUM_VAL' destination_name = 'TARGET_NUM' ) TO lt_mapping.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dyn_map_generic( ).
    lo_cut->map_any_structure( EXPORTING iv_source_data = ls_source it_mapping = lt_mapping CHANGING cs_target_data = ls_target ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-target_id exp = 'Custom ID' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_target-target_num exp = 111 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = ls_target-status exp = '' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die Verwendung von `cl_abap_corresponding` in einer generischen Methode, die `ANY` als Typ für Quell- und Zielstrukturen akzeptiert. Dies ist ein fortgeschrittenes Muster für die Entwicklung wiederverwendbarer und flexibler Mapping-Dienste. Die Möglichkeit, optional eine `SABP_DYN_MAP`-Tabelle zu übergeben, erhöht die Anpassungsfähigkeit der Methode erheblich und ist ein Kernmerkmal objektorientierten, dynamischen ABAP-Designs.
keywords: cl_abap_corresponding, dynamic programming, generic mapping, ANY, SABP_DYN_MAP, object orientation

Instructions: Ermitteln Sie die durchschnittliche Flugdauer für Flüge von 'LH' und 'AA' separat. Kombinieren Sie diese Durchschnittswerte in einer Ergebnismenge und fügen Sie eine Spalte hinzu, die angibt, ob die Dauer über oder unter einem globalen Durchschnitt liegt (hypothetisch).
hint: Verwenden Sie `UNION ALL` mit `AVG` und einer `CASE`-Anweisung oder einer nachfolgenden Verarbeitung mit `FOR`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sql_union_avg DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_avg_duration,
             carrid      TYPE sflight-carrid,
             avg_dur     TYPE f,
             duration_cat TYPE string,
           END OF ty_avg_duration.
    TYPES tt_avg_duration TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_avg_duration WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_avg_flight_duration
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_durations) TYPE tt_avg_duration.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sql_union_avg IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_avg_flight_duration.
    DATA: lv_global_avg TYPE f.

    " Hypothetischer globaler Durchschnitt (für Testzwecke)
    lv_global_avg = 300.0.

    SELECT carrid, AVG(fltime) AS avg_dur
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = 'LH'
      GROUP BY carrid
    UNION ALL
    SELECT carrid, AVG(fltime) AS avg_dur
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = 'AA'
      GROUP BY carrid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_raw_durations).

    rt_durations = VALUE #( FOR ls_raw IN lt_raw_durations
                             ( carrid       = ls_raw-carrid
                               avg_dur      = ls_raw-avg_dur
                               duration_cat = COND string(
                                 WHEN ls_raw-avg_dur > lv_global_avg THEN 'Above Global Avg'
                                 ELSE 'Below Global Avg'
                               )
                             )
                           ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_avg_flight_duration FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_avg_flight_duration.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sql_union_avg( ).
    DATA(lt_durations) = lo_cut->get_avg_flight_duration( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_durations ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte LH-Durchschnitt enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_durations[ carrid = 'LH' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte AA-Durchschnitt enthalten' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_durations[ carrid = 'AA' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Sollte Duration Category gefüllt sein' act = xsdbool( line_exists( lt_durations[ duration_cat IS NOT INITIAL ] ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel kombiniert `UNION ALL` mit Aggregatfunktionen (`AVG`) und einer nachfolgenden Datenverarbeitung mit einem `FOR`-Ausdruck. Der `FOR`-Ausdruck ist ein modernes ABAP-Konstrukt (ab 7.40), das eine kompakte und funktionale Art der Tabellenverarbeitung ermöglicht. Die `COND`-Anweisung innerhalb des `FOR`-Ausdrucks ist ebenfalls ein modernes Feature (ab 7.50) zur bedingten Wertzuweisung, was den Code sehr ausdrucksstark und effizient macht.
keywords: UNION, Open SQL, AVG, GROUP BY, FOR, COND, Data Analysis

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie einen String, der eine Zahl enthält, in einen Integer.

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie ein Datum in einen String im Format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONV` in Kombination mit String-Templates.
solution:
CLASS zcl_conv_date_to_str DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS convert_date_to_string
      IMPORTING
        id_date TYPE d
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_string) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_conv_date_to_str IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD convert_date_to_string.
    DATA(lv_iso_date) = CONV d( id_date ) DATE = ISO.
    rv_string = |{ lv_iso_date(4) }-{ lv_iso_date+4(2) }-{ lv_iso_date+6(2) }|.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_date_conversion FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_date_conversion.
    DATA(lo_converter) = NEW zcl_conv_date_to_str( ).
    DATA(ld_date) = sy-datum. " Current date
    DATA(lv_expected_string) = |{ ld_date(4) }-{ ld_date+4(2) }-{ ld_date+6(2) }|.
    DATA(lv_result) = lo_converter->convert_date_to_string( ld_date ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = lv_expected_string ).

    ld_date = '20231124'.
    lv_expected_string = '2023-11-24'.
    lv_result = lo_converter->convert_date_to_string( ld_date ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = lv_expected_string ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die Verwendung von `CONV` zur Umwandlung eines Datums in einen String im ISO-Format (YYYYMMDD) und anschließend die Formatierung mit String-Templates, um Bindestriche einzufügen. Dies ist eine prägnante Methode zur Datumsformatierung.
keywords: CONV, Date, String Templates, Type Conversion

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_data_source,
             field1 TYPE c LENGTH 10,

ABAP führt dabei eine feldweise Zuweisung durch, wobei auch implizite Konvertierungen (z.B. `c` zu `string`) vorgenommen werden. Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, indem Sie eine bestehende Tabelle transformieren und dabei Feldwerte mit `CONV` umwandeln.
hint: Nutzen Sie eine `FOR`-Expression in Kombination mit `CONV`.
solution:
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_flight_raw,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             price    TYPE s_price,
             currency TYPE s_currcode,
           END OF ty_s_flight_raw.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_flight_processed,
             carrier_id TYPE string,
             connection TYPE string,
             flight_date TYPE string,
             price_eur  TYPE decfloat16,
           END OF ty_s_flight_processed.

    TYPES ty_t_flight_raw      TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_s_flight_raw WITH EMPTY KEY.
    TYPES ty_t_flight_processed TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_s_flight_processed WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS zcl_conv_for_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
      PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS process_flights
          IMPORTING
            it_flights_raw TYPE ty_t_flight_raw
          RETURNING
            VALUE(rt_flights_processed) TYPE ty_t_flight_processed.
    ENDCLASS.

    CLASS zcl_conv_for_table IMPLEMENTATION.
      METHOD process_flights.
        rt_flights_processed = VALUE #( 
          FOR ls_raw IN it_flights_raw
            LET lv_iso_date = CONV d( ls_raw-fldate ) DATE = ISO IN
            ( carrier_id  = CONV string( ls_raw-carrid )
              connection  = CONV string( ls_raw-connid )
              flight_date = |{ lv_iso_date(4) }-{ lv_iso_date+4(2) }-{ lv_iso_date+6(2) }|
              price_eur   = CONV decfloat16( ls_raw-price ) ) 
        ).
      ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_flight_processing FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_flight_processing.
    DATA: lt_raw TYPE ty_t_flight_raw.
    APPEND INITIAL LINE TO lt_raw ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_raw>).
    <fs_raw>-carrid   = 'LH'.
    <fs_raw>-connid   = '0400'.
    <fs_raw>-fldate   = sy-datum.
    <fs_raw>-price    = '123.45'.
    <fs_raw>-currency = 'EUR'.

    DATA(lo_processor) = NEW zcl_conv_for_table( ).
    DATA(lt_processed) = lo_processor->process_flights( lt_raw ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_processed ) exp = 1 ).
    READ TABLE lt_processed INDEX 1 INTO DATA(ls_processed).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_processed-carrier_id exp = 'LH' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_processed-connection exp = '0400' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_processed-flight_date exp = |{ sy-datum(4) }-{ sy-datum+4(2) }-{ sy-datum+6(2) }| ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_processed-price_eur exp = '123.45' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die leistungsstarke Kombination von `FOR`-Expressions und dem `CONV`-Operator. Es ermöglicht die Transformation einer internen Tabelle in eine neue Tabelle, wobei Feldwerte während der Iteration und Zuweisung typsicher konvertiert werden. Dies führt zu sehr kompaktem und lesbarem Code für Tabellenoperationen.
keywords: CONV, FOR, VALUE, Internal Tables, Functional Programming, Type Conversion

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie den Inhalt eines generischen Feldsymbols (`ANY`) in einen spezifischen Typ (`string` oder `i`).
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONV` nach einer Zuweisung zu einem Feldsymbol.
solution:
CLASS zcl_conv_field_symbol DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_value_as_string
      IMPORTING
        ir_data TYPE REF TO data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_string) TYPE string.

    METHODS get_value_as_int
      IMPORTING
        ir_data TYPE REF TO data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_int) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_conv_field_symbol IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_value_as_string.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs_any> TYPE any.
    ASSIGN ir_data->* TO <fs_any>.

    IF <fs_any> IS ASSIGNED.
      rv_string = CONV string( <fs_any> ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_value_as_int.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs_any> TYPE any.

Instructions: Simulieren Sie Flugverspätungen für die `sflights`-Tabelle, indem Sie jedem Flug eine zufällige Verspätung zwischen 0 und 120 Minuten hinzufügen.
hint: Lesen Sie Daten aus `sflights`, verwenden Sie `cl_abap_random_int` und `FOR`-Expressions.
solution:
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_flight_delay,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             deptime  TYPE s_deptime,
             arrtime  TYPE s_arrtime,
             delay_min TYPE i,
           END OF ty_s_flight_delay.

    TYPES ty_t_flight_delay TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_s_flight_delay WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS zcl_random_flight_delay DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
      PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS simulate_delays
          IMPORTING
            iv_max_delay_min TYPE i DEFAULT 120
          RETURNING
            VALUE(rt_delayed_flights) TYPE ty_t_flight_delay.
    ENDCLASS.

    CLASS zcl_random_flight_delay IMPLEMENTATION.
      METHOD simulate_delays.
        DATA(lo_random) = cl_abap_random_int=>create( low = 0 high = iv_max_delay_min ).

        SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, deptime, arrtime
          FROM sflights
          INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights)
          UP TO 10 ROWS. " Limit for demo

        rt_delayed_flights = VALUE #( 
          FOR ls_flight IN lt_sflights
            LET lv_delay = lo_random->get_next( ) IN
            ( carrid    = ls_flight-carrid
              connid    = ls_flight-connid
              fldate    = ls_flight-fldate
              deptime   = ls_flight-deptime
              arrtime   = ls_flight-arrtime
              delay_min = lv_delay ) 
        ).
      ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_random_status_cond DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

        iv_max TYPE i DEFAULT 100

    DATA(lo_random) = cl_abap_random_int=>create(

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine interne Tabelle von Flugverbindungen aus `sflights` und fügen Sie jeder Verbindung eine zufällige 'Risikobewertung' (1-10) hinzu. Filtern Sie anschließend alle Verbindungen mit einer Bewertung unter 5 heraus.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_abap_random_int`, `FOR`-Expressions mit `VALUE` und `FILTER`.
solution:
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_flight_risk,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             fldate   TYPE s_date,
             risk_score TYPE i,
           END OF ty_s_flight_risk.

    TYPES ty_t_flight_risk TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_s_flight_risk WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS zcl_random_filter_flights DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
      PUBLIC SECTION.
        METHODS get_high_risk_flights
          RETURNING
            VALUE(rt_high_risk_flights) TYPE ty_t_flight_risk.
    ENDCLASS.

    CLASS zcl_random_filter_flights IMPLEMENTATION.
      METHOD get_high_risk_flights.
        DATA(lo_random) = cl_abap_random_int=>create( low = 1 high = 10 ).

        SELECT carrid, connid, fldate
          FROM sflights
          INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflights)
          UP TO 20 ROWS. " Limit for demo

        DATA(lt_all_flights_with_risk) = VALUE ty_t_flight_risk#( 
          FOR ls_flight IN lt_sflights
            ( carrid    = ls_flight-carrid
              connid    = ls_flight-connid
              fldate    = ls_flight-fldate
              risk_score = lo_random->get_next( ) ) 
        ).

        rt_high_risk_flights = FILTER #( lt_all_flights_with_risk USING KEY primary_key WHERE risk_score >= 5 ).
      ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

solution:
CLASS zcl_rel_create DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_object_key,
             objtype TYPE sibftypeid,
             objkey  TYPE sibfkey,
           END OF ty_object_key.
    METHODS create_relation
      IMPORTING
        iv_obj_a_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_a_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_obj_b_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_b_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_rel_type   TYPE sibfreltyp
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_success) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_create IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_relation.
    DATA(ls_object_a) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_a_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_a_key
    ).
    DATA(ls_object_b) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_b_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_b_key
    ).

    TRY.
        cl_binary_relation=>create_link(
          EXPORTING
            is_object_a = ls_object_a
            is_object_b = ls_object_b
            ip_reltype  = iv_rel_type
        ).
        rv_success = abap_true.
      CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
        " Log error or handle exception
        rv_success = abap_false.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Lesen Sie alle binären Verknüpfungen für ein gegebenes Business-Objekt und filtern Sie diese nach einem bestimmten Verknüpfungstyp. Nutzen Sie den `FILTER` Operator.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_binary_relation=>read_links` und anschließend den `FILTER` Operator auf der Ergebnistabelle.
solution:
CLASS zcl_rel_read DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_relation_info,
             objtype_a TYPE sibftypeid,
             objkey_a  TYPE sibfkey,
             objtype_b TYPE sibftypeid,
             objkey_b  TYPE sibfkey,
             reltype   TYPE sibfreltyp,
           END OF ty_relation_info.
    TYPES: tt_relation_info TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_relation_info WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_filtered_relations
      IMPORTING
        iv_obj_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_filter_rel_type TYPE sibfreltyp OPTIONAL
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_relations) TYPE tt_relation_info.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_read IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_filtered_relations.
    DATA(ls_object) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_key
    ).

    DATA: lt_links TYPE sibflinks.

    TRY.
        cl_binary_relation=>read_links(
          EXPORTING
            is_object = ls_object
          IMPORTING
            et_links  = lt_links
        ).

        IF iv_filter_rel_type IS NOT INITIAL.
          rt_relations = VALUE tt_relation_info(
            FOR ls_link IN FILTER #( lt_links USING KEY primary_key WHERE reltype = iv_filter_rel_type )
              (
                objtype_a = ls_link-objtype_a
                objkey_a  = ls_link-objkey_a
                objtype_b = ls_link-objtype_b
                objkey_b  = ls_link-objkey_b
                reltype   = ls_link-reltype
              )
          ).
        ELSE.
          rt_relations = VALUE tt_relation_info(
            FOR ls_link IN lt_links
              (
                objtype_a = ls_link-objtype_a
                objkey_a  = ls_link-objkey_a
                objtype_b = ls_link-objtype_b
                objkey_b  = ls_link-objkey_b
                reltype   = ls_link-reltype
              )
          ).
        ENDIF.

      CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
        " Log error, rt_relations will be empty
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie ein Tortendiagramm, das den prozentualen Anteil der Flüge pro Fluggesellschaft basierend auf der Tabelle `SFLIGHTS` anzeigt. Berechnen Sie die Prozentsätze mit dem `REDUCE` Operator.
hint: Aggregieren Sie zuerst die Flugzahlen, berechnen Sie die Gesamtzahl und dann die Prozentsätze mit `REDUCE`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_chart_pie DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_flight_percentage_chart
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_pie IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_flight_percentage_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_count,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             count  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_flight_count.
    TYPES: tt_flight_count TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_count WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_chart_pie_data,
             name  TYPE string,
             value TYPE f, " Use float for percentages
           END OF ty_chart_pie_data.
    TYPES: tt_chart_pie_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_chart_pie_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    " Aggregate data
    SELECT carrid, COUNT(*) AS count
      FROM sflight
      GROUP BY carrid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_flight_counts).

    " Calculate total count using REDUCE
    DATA(lv_total_flights) = REDUCE i(
      INIT sum = 0
      FOR ls_count IN lt_flight_counts
      NEXT sum = sum + ls_count-count
    ).

    " Prepare chart data with percentages using FOR and conditional logic
    DATA(lt_chart_data) = VALUE tt_chart_pie_data(
      FOR ls_flight_count IN lt_flight_counts
        (
          name = |{ ls_flight_count-carrid } ({ ( ls_flight_count-count * 100.0 ) / lv_total_flights }%)|
          value = ( ls_flight_count-count * 100.0 ) / lv_total_flights
        )
    ).

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_chart_type( cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_pie ).
    lo_chart->set_title( 'Fluganteil pro Fluggesellschaft' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data(
      EXPORTING
        i_series_name = 'Prozentsatz'
        it_data       = lt_chart_data
    ).
    lo_chart->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Löschen Sie eine spezifische binäre Verknüpfung zwischen zwei Business-Objekten, aber nur, wenn ein bestimmter Bedingungstyp erfüllt ist. Nutzen Sie den `COND` Operator für die Bedingungsprüfung.

CLASS zcl_rel_delete DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS delete_relation_conditionally
      IMPORTING
        iv_obj_a_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_a_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_obj_b_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_b_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_rel_type   TYPE sibfreltyp
        iv_condition_met TYPE abap_bool " Dummy condition for example
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_success) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_delete IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_relation_conditionally.
    DATA(ls_object_a) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_a_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_a_key
    ).
    DATA(ls_object_b) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_b_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_b_key
    ).

    rv_success = COND abap_bool(
      WHEN iv_condition_met = abap_true THEN
        TRY.
            cl_binary_relation=>delete_link(
              EXPORTING
                is_object_a = ls_object_a
                is_object_b = ls_object_b
                ip_reltype  = iv_rel_type
            ).
            abap_true
          CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
            " Log error
            abap_false
        ENDTRY
      ELSE
        abap_false " Condition not met, so no deletion
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_multi_line DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

    METHODS display_avg_flight_time_chart
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_multi_line IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_avg_flight_time_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_agg,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             fldate TYPE sflight-fldate,
             fltime TYPE sflight-fltime,
           END OF ty_flight_agg.
    TYPES: tt_flight_agg TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_agg WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_avg_time_by_month,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             month  TYPE c LENGTH 2,
             avg_time TYPE f,
           END OF ty_avg_time_by_month.
    TYPES: tt_avg_time_by_month TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_avg_time_by_month WITH EMPTY KEY.

    " Aggregate data: average flight time per airline per month
    SELECT carrid,
           SUBSTRING( fldate, 5, 2 ) AS month,
           AVG( fltime ) AS avg_time
      FROM sflight
      GROUP BY carrid, SUBSTRING( fldate, 5, 2 )
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_aggregated_data).

    " Group by carrid for multiple series
    DATA(lt_chart_series) = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_series(
      FOR GROUP OF ls_agg IN lt_aggregated_data BY ls_agg-carrid
      (
        name = ls_agg-carrid
        data = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_data(
          FOR ls_data IN GROUP ls_agg
            (
              name = ls_data-month
              value = ls_data-avg_time
            )
        )
      )
    ).

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_chart_type( cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_line ).
    lo_chart->set_title( 'Durchschnittliche Flugzeit pro Fluggesellschaft und Monat' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data_multiple(
      EXPORTING
        it_series_data = lt_chart_series
    ).
    lo_chart->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.

CLASS zcl_rel_exists DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS relation_exists
      IMPORTING
        iv_obj_a_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_a_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_obj_b_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_b_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_rel_type   TYPE sibfreltyp
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_exists) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_exists IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD relation_exists.
    DATA(ls_object_a) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_a_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_a_key
    ).
    DATA(ls_object_b) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_b_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_b_key
    ).

    DATA: lt_links TYPE sibflinks.

    TRY.
        cl_binary_relation=>read_links(
          EXPORTING
            is_object = ls_object_a
          IMPORTING
            et_links  = lt_links
        ).

        rv_exists = COND abap_bool(
          WHEN LINE_EXISTS( lt_links[
                                objtype_a = ls_object_a-objtype
                                objkey_a  = ls_object_a-objkey
                                objtype_b = ls_object_b-objtype
                                objkey_b  = ls_object_b-objkey
                                reltype   = iv_rel_type
                              ] ) THEN abap_true
          ELSE abap_false
        ).

      CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
        " Log error, rv_exists will be abap_false
        rv_exists = abap_false.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie ein Streudiagramm, das die Beziehung zwischen Flugzeit (`FLTIME`) und Entfernung (`DISTANCE`) für Flüge aus `SFLIGHTS` darstellt. Nutzen Sie den `FOR` Operator zur Datenaufbereitung.
hint: Verwenden Sie `SELECT` um die Daten zu holen und `FOR` um sie in das Chart-Format zu transformieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_chart_scatter DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_flight_scatter_chart
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_scatter IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_flight_scatter_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             fltime   TYPE sflight-fltime,
             distance TYPE sflight-distance,
           END OF ty_flight_data.
    TYPES: tt_flight_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    " Select relevant data
    SELECT fltime, distance
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_flights).

    " Prepare chart data using FOR
    DATA(lt_chart_data) = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_data(
      FOR ls_flight IN lt_flights
        (
          name = |Flug { sy-tabix }| " Dummy name for scatter points
          value = ls_flight-fltime
          value2 = ls_flight-distance " Use value2 for second axis in scatter
        )
    ).

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_chart_type( cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_scatter ).
    lo_chart->set_title( 'Flugzeit vs. Entfernung' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data(
      EXPORTING
        i_series_name = 'Flüge'
        it_data       = lt_chart_data
    ).
    lo_chart->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie ein Kombinationsdiagramm (Balken und Linie), das die Anzahl der Flüge pro Fluggesellschaft als Balken und die durchschnittliche Flugzeit als Linie darstellt. Nutzen Sie `SWITCH` für die dynamische Auswahl von Diagrammtypen pro Serie.
hint: Verwenden Sie `cl_gui_chart_engine=>set_series_data_multiple` und setzen Sie den `chart_type` innerhalb der `tt_series_data` dynamisch mit `SWITCH`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_chart_combo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_combo_chart
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_combo IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_combo_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_agg,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             flight_count TYPE i,
             avg_fltime TYPE f,
           END OF ty_flight_agg.
    TYPES: tt_flight_agg TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_agg WITH EMPTY KEY.

    " Aggregate data: flight count and average flight time per airline
    SELECT carrid,
           COUNT(*) AS flight_count,
           AVG( fltime ) AS avg_fltime
      FROM sflight
      GROUP BY carrid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_aggregated_data).

    " Prepare chart series data using FOR and SWITCH for dynamic chart type
    DATA(lt_chart_series) = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_series(
      FOR ls_agg IN lt_aggregated_data
        (
          name = ls_agg-carrid
          chart_type = SWITCH #( ls_agg-carrid
                                 WHEN 'LH' THEN cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_line " Example: LH as line
                                 WHEN 'AA' THEN cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_line " Example: AA as line
                                 ELSE cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_bar ) " Others as bars
          data = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_data(
            (
              name = 'Anzahl Flüge'
              value = ls_agg-flight_count
            )
            (
              name = 'Durchschnittszeit'
              value = ls_agg-avg_fltime
            )
          )
        )
    ).

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_title( 'Flugstatistik: Anzahl & Durchschnittszeit' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data_multiple(
      EXPORTING
        it_series_data = lt_chart_series
    ).
    lo_chart->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Zählen Sie die Anzahl der binären Verknüpfungen eines bestimmten Typs für ein gegebenes Business-Objekt. Nutzen Sie den `REDUCE` Operator.

CLASS zcl_rel_count DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS count_relations_by_type
      IMPORTING
        iv_obj_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_obj_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_rel_type TYPE sibfreltyp
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_count) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_count IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD count_relations_by_type.
    DATA(ls_object) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_obj_type
      objkey  = iv_obj_key
    ).

    DATA: lt_links TYPE sibflinks.

    TRY.
        cl_binary_relation=>read_links(
          EXPORTING
            is_object = ls_object
          IMPORTING
            et_links  = lt_links
        ).

        rv_count = REDUCE i(
          INIT count = 0
          FOR ls_link IN lt_links
            WHERE ( ls_link-reltype = iv_rel_type )
          NEXT count = count + 1
        ).

      CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
        " Log error, rv_count will be 0
        rv_count = 0.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_dyn_title DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_dynamic_title_chart
      IMPORTING
        io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container
        iv_carrid    TYPE sflight-carrid OPTIONAL.

CLASS zcl_chart_dyn_title IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_dynamic_title_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             count  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_flight_data.
    TYPES: tt_flight_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    DATA(lv_where_clause) = COND string(
      WHEN iv_carrid IS NOT INITIAL THEN |WHERE carrid = '{ iv_carrid }'|
      ELSE ''
    ).

    " Dynamic SQL to filter by carrid if provided
    SELECT carrid, COUNT(*) AS count
      FROM sflight
      &lv_where_clause
      GROUP BY carrid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_flight_counts).

    DATA(lt_chart_data) = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_data(
      FOR ls_flight_count IN lt_flight_counts
        (
          name = ls_flight_count-carrid
          value = ls_flight_count-count
        )
    ).

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_chart_type( cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_bar ).
    lo_chart->set_title( 'Flüge pro Fluggesellschaft' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data(
      EXPORTING
        i_series_name = 'Anzahl Flüge'
        it_data       = lt_chart_data
    ).
    lo_chart->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Extrahieren Sie alle Schlüssel der mit einem Quellobjekt verbundenen Zielobjekte eines bestimmten Typs. Nutzen Sie `FOR` und `COND` für die Transformation.
hint: Lesen Sie die Verknüpfungen und verwenden Sie dann `FOR` mit `COND` um die Zielobjektschlüssel zu extrahieren.
solution:
CLASS zcl_rel_get_keys DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_target_object_keys
      IMPORTING
        iv_source_obj_type TYPE sibftypeid
        iv_source_obj_key  TYPE sibfkey
        iv_rel_type        TYPE sibfreltyp
        iv_target_obj_type TYPE sibftypeid
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_target_keys) TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sibfkey WITH EMPTY KEY.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rel_get_keys IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_target_object_keys.
    DATA(ls_source_object) = VALUE sibflporb(
      objtype = iv_source_obj_type
      objkey  = iv_source_obj_key
    ).

    DATA: lt_links TYPE sibflinks.

    TRY.
        cl_binary_relation=>read_links(
          EXPORTING
            is_object = ls_source_object
          IMPORTING
            et_links  = lt_links
        ).

        rt_target_keys = VALUE #(
          FOR ls_link IN lt_links
            WHERE ( ls_link-reltype = iv_rel_type )
            ( COND #(
                WHEN ls_link-objtype_a = iv_source_obj_type AND ls_link-objkey_a = iv_source_obj_key
                     AND ls_link-objtype_b = iv_target_obj_type THEN
                  ls_link-objkey_b
                WHEN ls_link-objtype_b = iv_source_obj_type AND ls_link-objkey_b = iv_source_obj_key
                     AND ls_link-objtype_a = iv_target_obj_type THEN
                  ls_link-objkey_a
                ELSE
                  THROW cx_abap_invalid_value( ) " Should not happen with correct WHERE clause
              )
            )
        ).

      CATCH cx_binary_relation INTO DATA(lx_rel).
        " Log error, rt_target_keys will be empty
      CATCH cx_abap_invalid_value.
        " Handle unexpected condition if THROW is reached
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

    " Pre-requisite: Create dummy relations
    DATA(lo_create) = NEW zcl_rel_create( ).
    lo_create->create_relation( 'BUS1001' '000000000000000011' 'BUS2000120' '0000000011' 'ATTA' ).
    lo_create->create_relation( 'BUS1001' '000000000000000011' 'BUS2000120' '0000000012' 'ATTA' ).
    lo_create->create_relation( 'BUS1001' '000000000000000011' 'BUS1001' '0000000000000013' 'NOTE' ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_rel_get_keys( ).
    DATA(lt_keys) = lo_cut->get_target_object_keys(
      iv_source_obj_type = 'BUS1001'
      iv_source_obj_key  = '000000000000000011'
      iv_rel_type        = 'ATTA'
      iv_target_obj_type = 'BUS2000120'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_keys ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( xsdbool( line_exists( lt_keys[ table_line = '0000000011' ] ) ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( xsdbool( line_exists( lt_keys[ table_line = '0000000012' ] ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_get_target_keys_no_match.
    " Pre-requisite: Relations from previous test
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_rel_get_keys( ).
    DATA(lt_keys) = lo_cut->get_target_object_keys(
      iv_source_obj_type = 'BUS1001'
      iv_source_obj_key  = '000000000000000011'
      iv_rel_type        = 'ATTA'
      iv_target_obj_type = 'BUS1001' " No ATTA relations to BUS1001
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( lt_keys ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_get_target_keys_no_relations.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_rel_get_keys( ).
    DATA(lt_keys) = lo_cut->get_target_object_keys(
      iv_source_obj_type = 'BUS1001'
      iv_source_obj_key  = 'NONEXISTENT_SOURCE_2'
      iv_rel_type        = 'ATTA'
      iv_target_obj_type = 'BUS2000120'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( lt_keys ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FOR` Operator wird verwendet, um die gelesenen Verknüpfungen zu iterieren und zu filtern. Innerhalb des `FOR`-Ausdrucks wird `COND` eingesetzt, um den korrekten Zielobjektschlüssel zu extrahieren, basierend darauf, ob das Quellobjekt Objekt A oder Objekt B in der Verknüpfung ist und ob der Zielobjekttyp übereinstimmt. CLASS zcl_chart_dyn_axis DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.

        iv_unit      TYPE string OPTIONAL.

CLASS zcl_chart_dyn_axis IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_dynamic_axis_chart.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             count  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_flight_data.
    TYPES: tt_flight_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    SELECT carrid, COUNT(*) AS count
      FROM sflight
      GROUP BY carrid
      INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_flight_counts).

    DATA(lt_chart_data) = VALUE cl_gui_chart_engine=>tt_data(
      FOR ls_flight_count IN lt_flight_counts
        (
          name = ls_flight_count-carrid
          value = ls_flight_count-count

    DATA(lo_chart) = NEW cl_gui_chart_engine(
      i_parent = io_container
    ).

    lo_chart->set_chart_type( cl_gui_chart_engine=>co_type_bar ).
    lo_chart->set_title( 'Flüge pro Fluggesellschaft' ).
    lo_chart->set_series_data(
      EXPORTING
        i_series_name = 'Anzahl Flüge'
        it_data       = lt_chart_data
    ).

    " Dynamic Y-axis label using String Templates and COND
    DATA(lv_y_axis_label) = COND string(
      WHEN iv_unit IS NOT INITIAL THEN |Anzahl Flüge ({ iv_unit })|
      ELSE 'Anzahl Flüge'

Instructions: Erstellen Sie dynamisch ein Datenobjekt basierend auf einem übergebenen Typnamen und weisen Sie ihm einen Wert zu. Geben Sie den Wert als String zurück.
hint: Nutzen Sie CL_ABAP_TYPEDESCR=>DESCRIBE_BY_NAME, CREATE DATA und Feld-Symbole.
solution:
CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_data DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS create_and_set_data
      IMPORTING
        iv_type_name TYPE string
        iv_value     TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_data IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_and_set_data.
    DATA lo_typedescr TYPE REF TO cl_abap_typedescr.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS <fs_data> TYPE any.

    TRY.
        lo_typedescr = cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_name( iv_type_name ).
        CREATE DATA DATA(lr_data) TYPE HANDLE lo_typedescr.
        ASSIGN lr_data->* TO <fs_data>.

        IF <fs_data> IS ASSIGNED.
          <fs_data> = iv_value.
          rv_result = |Dynamisch erstelltes Objekt vom Typ { iv_type_name } mit Wert: { <fs_data> }|.
        ELSE.
          rv_result = |Fehler: Datenobjekt konnte nicht zugewiesen werden.|.
        ENDIF.

      CATCH cx_sy_unknown_type.
        rv_result = |Fehler: Typ '{ iv_type_name }' ist unbekannt.|.
      CATCH cx_sy_assign_error.
        rv_result = |Fehler: Wert '{ iv_value }' konnte nicht zugewiesen werden.|.
      CATCH cx_sy_create_data_error.
        rv_result = |Fehler: Datenobjekt konnte nicht erstellt werden.|.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
